# everpure_azure_virtual_machine_connection (Resource)

Connects an Azure virtual machine to one or more Everpure Volume Groups over iSCSI. The connection is made by the PureStorage.Extensions iSCSI mount VM extension, which this resource installs on the virtual machine and configures with the Volume Groups' iSCSI endpoints.

Use one connection resource per virtual machine: Azure rejects a second instance of the extension on the same virtual machine. If the virtual machine was already connected through the Azure Portal or the API, [import](#import) its existing extension instead of creating a new one.

~> **This resource takes over the virtual machine's iSCSI connections, and is incompatible with connections managed any other way.** Every apply connects the virtual machine to exactly `volume_group_ids` and overrides iSCSI connections made outside this resource.

~> **Connecting a virtual machine to a Volume Group that has no volumes fails.** Referencing the Volume Group's `id` in `volume_group_ids` only orders the connection after the Volume Group, not after its volumes, so Terraform can create the connection while the Volume Group is still empty. Add every volume the virtual machine should see to the connection's `depends_on`, as in the example below: a volume created after the connection is not visible on the virtual machine until its iSCSI sessions are rescanned by hand.

To configure iSCSI on the virtual machine yourself instead (your own initiator setup, cloud-init, configuration management), don't use this resource: read the Volume Group's portal IPs, ports and IQN from the [`everpure_azure_volume_group_connection_parameters` data source](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/PureStorage-OpenConnect/everpure-azure/latest/docs/data-sources/volume_group_connection_parameters).

~> **Destroying this resource logs every iSCSI session out before removing the extension**, but leaves any OS-level configuration behind (installed packages, `multipath.conf`, udev rules).

Required Azure role assignments: `Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines/read`, `Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines/extensions/read`, `Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines/extensions/write`, `Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines/extensions/delete` and `PureStorage.Block/storagePools/volumeGroups/listConnectionParameters/action`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    everpure = {
      source = "PureStorage-OpenConnect/everpure-azure"
    }
  }
}

provider "everpure" {
  subscription_id = var.subscription_id
}

variable "subscription_id" {
  type = string
}

variable "storage_pool_id" {
  type        = string
  description = "Full ARM ID of an existing Everpure Storage Pool in the same subscription."
}

variable "linux_virtual_machine_id" {
  type        = string
  description = "Full ARM ID of an existing Linux virtual machine that can reach the storage pool's subnet."
}

variable "windows_virtual_machine_id" {
  type        = string
  description = "Full ARM ID of an existing Windows virtual machine that can reach the storage pool's subnet."
}

resource "everpure_azure_volume_group" "example" {
  name            = "vg-prod-east"
  storage_pool_id = var.storage_pool_id
}

resource "everpure_azure_volume" "example" {
  name                    = "vol-data"
  volume_group_id         = everpure_azure_volume_group.example.id
  provisioned_size_in_gib = 100
}

resource "everpure_azure_virtual_machine_connection" "linux" {
  virtual_machine_id = var.linux_virtual_machine_id
  volume_group_ids = [
    everpure_azure_volume_group.example.id,
  ]

  # Connecting to a volume group that has no volumes fails, and
  # volume_group_ids alone does not wait for the volume to be created.
  depends_on = [
    everpure_azure_volume.example,
  ]
}

resource "everpure_azure_virtual_machine_connection" "windows" {
  virtual_machine_id = var.windows_virtual_machine_id
  volume_group_ids = [
    everpure_azure_volume_group.example.id,
  ]

  depends_on = [
    everpure_azure_volume.example,
  ]

  # First-time setup on Windows needs a reboot to finish. Without this, the
  # apply ends with a warning and the VM has to be rebooted by hand.
  reboot_allowed = true
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `virtual_machine_id` (String) Full ARM ID of the virtual machine (`Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines`). Can be in a different subscription than the one configured on the provider; if that subscription is in another Microsoft Entra tenant, list the tenant in the provider's `auxiliary_tenant_ids`. Changing this value replaces the resource: the extension is removed from the old virtual machine and created on the new one.
- `volume_group_ids` (Set of String) Full ARM IDs of the Volume Groups to connect this virtual machine to. Each Volume Group's iSCSI endpoints (portal IPs and target IQNs) are resolved automatically and sent to the extension; order does not matter. Changing this set logs out sessions for any Volume Group removed from it and connects sessions for any Volume Group added to it, without disturbing the rest.

### Optional

- `extension_name` (String) Name of the VM extension instance. Defaults to `PureMountIscsi` on create — the same name the Azure Portal's "Mount on Virtual Machine" action uses, so a later Portal-driven mount of the same virtual machine updates this instance instead of failing. Set this to a distinct name to make a Portal mount fail instead of silently taking over this resource's extension instance. On import, this attribute is set to the imported extension's existing name. Changing this attribute after creation replaces the resource: the extension is deleted (disconnecting every session) and recreated under the new name.
- `initiator_name` (String) iSCSI initiator name (IQN) to configure on the virtual machine. Left unset, the virtual machine keeps its OS-generated initiator name, which this provider cannot read back (it never appears in Azure Resource Manager), so this attribute reads back as unset even when the guest has one. Setting this attribute, or changing it, changes the virtual machine's iSCSI identity and logs out its existing sessions before reconnecting under the new name.
- `iscsi_session_count` (Number) Number of iSCSI sessions per portal to establish for each connected target. Defaults to 2 (the extension's own default). Applies only to Volume Groups connected after this value changes; targets already connected keep their current session count. Must be between 1 and 16. Can be changed in place.
- `reapply_on_boot` (Block List) Configures whether the extension reapplies its iSCSI configuration on every virtual machine boot. Omitting this block is equivalent to `{ enabled = false }`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--reapply_on_boot))
- `reboot_allowed` (Boolean) Whether the virtual machine may be rebooted automatically while this extension configures it. Defaults to `false`. Can be changed in place. Effective on Windows only:

* On Windows, first-time iSCSI setup (MPIO) cannot finish without a reboot. With this attribute left `false` (the default), that first setup reports success with a warning telling you to reboot the virtual machine, or set this attribute to `true`, before configuration finishes; the resource is not marked failed. The warning repeats on every plan or refresh until the virtual machine is rebooted and the extension reports configuration complete.
* On Linux this attribute has no effect.
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))
- `windows_settings` (Block List) Advanced settings honoured on Windows virtual machines only; ignored on Linux. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--windows_settings))

### Read-Only

- `extension_type` (String) The extension type installed: `MountIscsiLinux` or `MountIscsiWindows`, derived from the virtual machine's operating system. Changing this value (the virtual machine's operating system changing) replaces the resource.
- `id` (String) Full ARM ID of the VM extension (`Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines/{vm}/extensions/{name}`).
- `resolved_targets` (Attributes List) The iSCSI targets (IP, port and IQN) resolved from `volume_group_ids` and configured on the virtual machine. Populated automatically; recomputed whenever `volume_group_ids` or a referenced Volume Group's connection endpoints change. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--resolved_targets))

<a id="nestedblock--reapply_on_boot"></a>
### Nested Schema for `reapply_on_boot`

Required:

- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the extension reapplies its configuration on every boot.

Optional:

- `reboot_on_reapply_allowed` (Boolean) Whether the virtual machine may be rebooted automatically if reapplying the configuration on boot requires it (Windows only). Defaults to `false`.


<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) Defaults to 30 minutes. A duration string: a number with a unit suffix s (seconds), m (minutes) or h (hours); segments can be combined, e.g. "30m" or "1h30m". Used when creating the virtual machine connection.
- `delete` (String) Defaults to 15 minutes. A duration string: a number with a unit suffix s (seconds), m (minutes) or h (hours); segments can be combined, e.g. "30m" or "1h30m". Used when destroying the virtual machine connection.
- `read` (String) Defaults to 5 minutes. A duration string: a number with a unit suffix s (seconds), m (minutes) or h (hours); segments can be combined, e.g. "30m" or "1h30m". Used when reading the virtual machine connection.
- `update` (String) Defaults to 30 minutes. A duration string: a number with a unit suffix s (seconds), m (minutes) or h (hours); segments can be combined, e.g. "30m" or "1h30m". Used when updating the virtual machine connection.


<a id="nestedblock--windows_settings"></a>
### Nested Schema for `windows_settings`

Optional:

- `disk_timeout_in_seconds` (Number) MPIO disk I/O timeout in seconds. Leaving this unset sends 0, which keeps the extension's own default (240 seconds).
- `link_down_time_in_seconds` (Number) MPIO link-down time in seconds. Leaving this unset sends 0, which keeps the extension's own default (180 seconds).


<a id="nestedatt--resolved_targets"></a>
### Nested Schema for `resolved_targets`

Read-Only:

- `ip` (String) Portal IP address of the target.
- `iqn` (String) IQN of the target, unique to the Volume Group it was resolved from.
- `port` (Number) Portal port of the target.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `identity` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = everpure_azure_virtual_machine_connection.app
  identity = {
    subscription_id      = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"
    resource_group_name  = "rg-app"
    virtual_machine_name = "vm-app01"
    name                 = "MountIscsiLinux-deploy" # the extension name
  }
}

resource "everpure_azure_virtual_machine_connection" "app" {
  # ... configuration matching the imported connection
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
### Identity Schema

#### Required

- `name` (String) Name of the virtual machine extension.
- `resource_group_name` (String) Name of the resource group the resource lives in.
- `subscription_id` (String) Azure subscription ID the resource lives in.
- `virtual_machine_name` (String) Name of the virtual machine the extension is installed on.

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Virtual machine connections are imported by the full Azure resource ID of
# the underlying VM extension. volume_group_ids cannot be recovered from the
# extension's settings, so it is left unset after import; the first plan
# shows it being set from configuration.
terraform import everpure_azure_virtual_machine_connection.app \
  "/subscriptions/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000/resourceGroups/rg-app/providers/Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines/vm-app01/extensions/PureMountIscsi"
```
